references.text: Describes Israel's route from the Wilderness of Sin to Rephidim as part of the complete list of camp locations in the wilderness.
The previous camp location in the Wilderness of Sin, from which the congregation of Israel now breaks camp.
Explains what it means that Israel traveled 'by the Lord's command' - they followed the pillar of cloud.
The place Rephidim receives the names Massah and Meribah because of the lack of water mentioned in this verse.
Moses reminds the people of the lack of water in the wilderness and how God gave them water from the rock.
The psalm describes how God gave the people water in the wilderness despite the shortage.
A poetic reference to the water that flowed from the rock in the wilderness.
A prophetic reflection on how the people did not thirst when God led them through the wilderness and provided water from the rock.
Paul refers to the spiritual rock that followed Israel and gave them drink in the wilderness.
Continues the same route from Rephidim to the Wilderness of Sinai, linking the water crisis to the upcoming covenant meeting.
Confirms the same historical event (arrival at Rephidim and lack of water) from another book.
Describes the immediate continuation of the route after the events at Rephidim.
Reaffirms the theological principle that journeys and camp locations occur solely by the Lord's command.
Highlights the general discipline and obedience to the Lord's command that characterized the entire exodus.
